sources.title: Causal Inference: What If
sources.publisher: Chapman & Hall/CRC; author-hosted copy at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
sources.locator: Chapter 1, p. 12, “A definition of causal effect”
sources.scope: Defines causal effects as contrasts under alternative treatments in a target population and distinguishes causal from associational quantities.
sources.boundary: Does not establish identification for a particular dataset, the validity of a causal model, or an effect estimate.

sources.title: PERK specification
sources.scope: Defines commitment algorithms, correctness, computational hiding, and computational binding.
sources.boundary: A candidate submission hosted by NIST is not a NIST standard or endorsement and does not establish security of an implementation.

sources.title: DLMF §3.1 — Arithmetics and Error Measures
sources.scope: Defines floating-point representation and rounding conventions.
sources.boundary: Does not establish bit-for-bit deterministic results across hardware, compilers, libraries, execution order, or implementations.

sources.title: The International System of Units (SI Brochure)
sources.scope: Defines dimensions of base and derived quantities and their expression as products of base dimensions.
sources.boundary: Does not validate a particular equation, measurement, unit conversion, or uncertainty budget.

sources.title: Formal verification
sources.publisher: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures
sources.scope: Defines formal verification through formal requirements, a model, logic, and rules of inference.
sources.boundary: Does not establish that a particular model matches the implemented system or that a particular proof is sound.

sources.title: DLMF §3.3 — Interpolation
sources.scope: Defines polynomial interpolation through distinct nodes and identifies other interpolation methods.
sources.boundary: Does not establish accuracy between nodes, suitability for extrapolation, or numerical stability for a particular implementation.

sources.title: DLMF §3.1(ii) — Interval Arithmetic
sources.scope: Defines interval arithmetic as producing inclusion regions and states the restriction on division by an interval containing zero.
sources.boundary: Does not certify an interval implementation, a rounding mode, or the tightness of a computed bound.

sources.title: IEEE 1788-2015 — Standard for Interval Arithmetic
sources.version: 2015 standard; landing page observed as inactive-reserved
sources.locator: Public standard landing page: Abstract and Scope
sources.scope: Confirms the identity and stated scope of the interval-arithmetic standard.
sources.boundary: The full subscribed standard was not inspected; this source cannot supply clause-level normative requirements.

sources.title: DLMF §3.5 — Quadrature
sources.scope: Defines interpolatory quadrature with weights and an error term and states its polynomial exactness.
sources.boundary: Does not establish convergence or error for an arbitrary integrand, node choice, or numerical implementation.

sources.title: A Methodology for Numerical Software Testing
sources.scope: Distinguishes an ill-conditioned problem from an unstable algorithm and bounds stability by comparison with inherent error.
sources.boundary: Does not establish the stability of a named algorithm without an analysis under its stated inputs and arithmetic.

sources.title: Convex Optimization
sources.publisher: Cambridge University Press; author-hosted copy at Stanford
sources.scope: Defines a standard optimization problem using an objective, inequality and equality constraints, feasible points, and optimal value.
sources.boundary: Does not establish convexity, existence or uniqueness of a solution, or performance of a solver for a particular problem.

sources.title: IERS Conventions (2010), Chapter 5
sources.publisher: International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service
sources.locator: Chapter 5, transformation between the ITRS and GCRS
sources.scope: Specifies the sequence and quantities used to transform between terrestrial and celestial reference systems.
sources.boundary: Does not establish that a software implementation uses the correct epoch, Earth-orientation parameters, units, or convention version.

sources.title: DLMF §3.8 — Nonlinear Equations
sources.scope: Defines bracketing and iterative methods for locating zeros, with conditions and accuracy or conditioning considerations.
sources.boundary: Does not establish convergence for an arbitrary starting value or certify a computed root without residual and conditioning evidence.
